headline: Garmin Marq Captain smartwatch now 66% off at $750
summary: Originally priced at over $3,200, this premium smartwatch features a titanium case, sapphire crystal display, and 16-day battery life.
details: Garmin's Marq series offers a high-end smartwatch experience, blending sleek design with premium materials. The Marq Captain model is currently available for a significant discount, dropping from over $3,200 to just $750.
This particular model boasts a domed sapphire crystal display, a titanium case and bezel, and a 1.2-inch AMOLED screen. It offers an impressive battery life of up to 16 days on a single charge.

As a Garmin device, it includes comprehensive health and fitness tracking, such as heart rate, Pulse Ox, sleep, and stress monitoring. It also provides navigation data, maps, and features for training assistance.
The Marq Captain is specifically designed for seafaring, with unique functionalities like regatta timing, stream data, and autopilot control when paired with compatible marine hardware.
Beyond its specialized features, users can also download music from supported services, make contactless payments with Garmin Pay, and access golf course and ski resort maps.

headline_marked: [[Android 17]] protects privacy by default, reducing user prompts
headline: Android 17 protects privacy by default, reducing user prompts
summary: The latest Android version shifts privacy controls to automatic protection, aiming to safeguard users from accidental oversharing and potential security risks.
details: Android 17 is introducing a new approach to privacy, where many protections are active by default rather than requiring user intervention. This aims to simplify the user experience and prevent common mistakes made during app setup or daily use.

The system now automatically prevents apps from accessing sensitive information like SMS OTPs unless they are explicitly linked to the originating domain. This protection extends to WebOTP messages, ensuring one-time passwords are not quietly read by unauthorized applications.
For standard SMS verification codes, Android 17 enforces boundaries by knowing which apps or websites the code belongs to, removing the need for users to manually manage these permissions each time.

Security features like Theft Detection Lock and Remote Lock are now enabled by default on devices running Android 17. This ensures that crucial protections are active immediately, even in stressful situations like a phone being stolen.
Android 17 also introduces stricter limits on PIN and password guess attempts, increasing the delay between tries to make brute-force attacks more difficult and giving users time to react.

While automatic protection is enhanced, Android 17 still allows users to review and customize settings. The OS aims to explain blocked actions and provide options for legitimate features that might be affected.
The OS also respects user control for highly sensitive permissions like precise location, contacts, microphone, and camera, ensuring these still require explicit user decisions.
New features include a privacy-focused contact picker that allows sharing specific details instead of the entire address book, and a system location button for precise, session-based access.
An optional Advanced Protection mode is available for users who want even stricter security rules, though it may impact daily usability and requires a deliberate choice to enable.
